αὐτὸν ἡδονῇ· εὔψυχος δέ ἐστι πάσαις αὐτὸς εἰς ἀγάπην· οὕτως τῷ πάντων Θεῷ αἱ
τῶν ἀγγέλων τάξεις, οὐ μόνον φόβῳ, ἀλλὰ καὶ 17.233 ἀγάπῃ ὑπείκουσιν, ὅτε θέλει
αὐτὸς νοεῖν αὐτὰς τὸ πρόσταγμα αὑτοῦ καὶ ποιεῖν· ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ περὶ ταῖς τῶν
δικαίων ψυχαῖς πέφυκεν· ὅσαι γὰρ ὑπό κεινται τῷ προστάγματι αὐτοῦ, οὐ μόνον τὰ
ἐν ταῖς Γραφαῖς ἐναποκείμενα μυστήρια καὶ βάθη εὐδοκεῖ γινώσκειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅσα
ἐν τῷ βίῳ πέφυκε γίνεσθαι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, παρὰ ἀνθρώπων τε καὶ δαιμόνων, ἢ δι'
ὁράσεως νοὸς, χάριτι θείου Πνεύματος παρέχει πρόγνωσιν, ἢ δι' ἀγγέλου μύησιν, ἢ
δι' ὁράματος ἀπο κάλυψιν. ∆υνάστας ἐνταῦθα τοὺς δικαίους φησὶν, οἵτινες κατὰ τῶν
δαιμόνων καὶ τῶν παθῶν τὴν δύναμιν ἔχον τες, ἥντινα θυμὸν ἐκάλεσε· μὴ
πινέτωσαν ἐκ τοῦ τὸν νοῦν μεθύσκοντος, καὶ τὰς φρένας θολοῦντος ὀξώδους οἴνου
τῶν αἱρετικῶν, τοῦ κατὰ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ σοφίας γνώσεώς τι ἔχοντος· ἵνα μὴ πιόντες,

pass_a_gloss: He finds joy in delight; yet he is stout-hearted and directs himself wholly to love in every respect. Thus, the angelic ranks submit to the God of all—not merely in fear, but also in love—when He wills to perceive them as they obey His decree and carry it out. Similarly, it is inherent in the souls of the just to be thus inclined: for all who submit to His command do not only wish to know the mysteries and depths treasured in the Scriptures, which He approves of being known, but also whatever is destined to happen in human life—whether caused by men or demons, whether through intellectual insight, by the gift of the divine Spirit granting foresight, or through angelic teaching, or through the unveiling of a vision. Here he terms the just "forces," those who wield power against demons and passions, which he calls "spirit." Let them not drink from the bowl that maddens the mind and muddles the senses with the biting wine of heretics, which holds some knowledge opposed to God’s wisdom; lest, having drunk, they lose God’s wisdom and cannot judge soundly or comprehend the theory of knowledge, and thus fail to aid themselves and the weaker in spirit. To those who grieve in sin and unawareness, give them to drink from the Lord’s vineyard to the point of drunkenness—that is, fasting, prayer, temperance, confession, and all things that gladden the soul; but to those in leadership, let them drink the aches of sin to satiety, so that, having drunk, they may forget the demonic lack. For the one who is drunk on the Lord’s knowledge forgets the exercise of sorrows. He names the needy the one stripped of knowledge. Sin defiles; the spiritual word kills the old self ruled by deceitful lusts, setting the mind right in righteousness—this mind is God’s throne, where wisdom and understanding naturally dwell, nowhere else. Righteousness without rational nature is unreal. All this is Christ. Be genuine, not pretentious: don’t boast, stay quiet among the wise, listen to elders. Never claim, “I’ll exalt my throne above the stars, equal the Highest.” Don’t seek the highest seat; aim for the lowest. Better to hear “Come up” than be shamed, told to take last place. Don’t fake wisdom or self-righteousness—let others praise you. So God raised him high, gave the supreme name. He recalls: God is our friend, becoming man for love of us; he told disciples, “I call you friends, not slaves.” If a friend rebukes you, Christ says: avoid that sin, don’t scorn the correction, retreat and return to first prudence—God’s mercy. He urges: thank God’s laws; friendship means loving God and neighbor. Whoever loves God must guard these inwardly, lest he become divided and tormented in God’s sight. Each gets what they deserve; Jesus told believing Jews that staying in his word makes true disciples, and truth frees from law’s curse. Since friendship and Christ both liberate, and Christ is truth and friendship, all who know Christ are mutual friends. Only in this friendship: same-person friends are friends, and others too. The virtue-taught keeper safeguards his goods agreeably. Put a costly sardian in a gold ear, and Lord’s wisdom in a calm, listening mind. Like snowmelt water in desert heat aiding and cooling the burned, God helps those receiving his knowledge, wisdom, and laws. As snow melts under heat, so just advice melts soul’s wickedness. Like winds and clouds steering ships to avoid wreck, false knowledge in wisdom keeps God’s-wise from ruin with boasters. As bones give body strength and safety, virtues grow in soul naturally. But these bones break if sins unguarded; some name the passionate soul frail, as it shatters its own spiritual bones toward God.

He rejoices in pleasure; yet he is of good courage and turns himself wholly toward love in all things. Thus, the orders of the angels submit to the God of all, not only in fear but also in love, when He wills to perceive them as they obey His command and act upon it. Likewise, it is natural for the souls of the righteous to be so disposed: for all who place themselves under His command do not merely desire to know the mysteries and depths hidden in the Scriptures, which He approves of being known, but also whatever is destined to occur in human life—whether brought about by men or demons, whether through mental vision, by the grace of the divine Spirit granting foreknowledge, or through angelic instruction, or through the revelation of a vision. Here he calls the righteous "powers," those who possess strength against demons and passions, which he terms "spirit." Let them not drink from the cup that intoxicates the mind and clouds the senses with the harsh wine of heretics, which contains some knowledge contrary to the wisdom of God; lest, having drunk, they forget God’s wisdom and be unable to judge rightly or perceive the theory of knowledge, and thus fail to help themselves and the weaker in soul. To those who mourn in sin and ignorance, give them to drink from the Lord’s vineyard unto intoxication—that is, fasting, prayer, self-control, confession, and all things that bring joy to the soul; but to those in positions of authority, let them drink the pains of sin unto satisfaction, so that, having drunk, they may forget the demonic poverty. For the one who is intoxicated by the knowledge of the Lord forgets the practice of sorrows. He calls the poor the one deprived of knowledge.

Now then, concerning the corrupt and impure nature brought about by sin: the one who, through the spiritual word, puts to death the old man corrupted by deceitful desires, establishes his own mind in righteousness. This mind is said to be the throne of God, for wisdom and understanding have no other natural dwelling place but here; they do not sit elsewhere by nature. And righteousness, if not grounded in rational nature, cannot truly exist. All these things—the spiritual word, the renewed mind, righteousness, wisdom, understanding—are none other than Christ himself. You must be what you appear to be; do not pretend. Do not boast, but remain silent among the wise and listen attentively to the elders. Do not say, “I will set my throne above the stars, and I will be like the Most High.” Do not crave the chief seats, but fix your gaze on the lowest place. For it is better to be told, “Come up here,” than to be told, “Take the lowest place,” and be sent away in shame before the powerful. Do not pretend to be wise, nor deem yourself just. It is better that good things be spoken of you than that you speak them yourself. Therefore, God exalted him highly and bestowed on him the name above every name. He speaks of what has come before: our friend is God, who, because of his friendship toward us, became human. For he himself said to the disciples, “I no longer call you servants, but friends.” When a friend rebukes you, Christ says, because of this sin, avoid it; do not despise the rebuke, but withdraw and return to the original sound judgment—that is, to God’s loving kindness. He says, give thanks for God’s commandments; and friendship, he says, is the love toward God and neighbor. Let the one who loves God keep these commands within himself, so that he may not become twofold in distress before God.

When each receives what is due according to their worth, the Savior also says in the Gospels to the Jews who believed in him: If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples, and the truth has freed you from the curse of the law. Therefore, if friendship liberates, and the Savior liberates, and Christ is both truth and friendship, it follows that all who possess knowledge of Christ are friends to one another. Thus, concerning this friendship alone, those who are friends of the same person are friends, and others are also friends. The one who has been taught about the virtues and practices them guards his own possessions in a harmonious and mutually beneficial way. Place a precious sardius stone into a golden earlobe, and the wisdom of the Lord into an understanding that is impassive yet obedient to the Lord. Just as water flowing from snow in a dry place under heat brings benefit and refreshes the scorched, so God acts upon those who receive his knowledge, wisdom, and commandments. And just as snow melts under heat, so too does the counsel of the just dissolve the wickedness of the soul. As winds and clouds guide sailors upon the sea to prevent shipwreck, so the false knowledge of those in God’s wisdom prevents them from perishing along with those who boast in it. As bones give strength and security to the body, so the virtues have grown naturally within the soul. Yet these bones are shattered if not guarded against sins; some have called the spirited soul weak, for it breaks its own spiritual bones before God.
